docs.title: Workout Journal
docs.text:
My running and cycling journal: each session's numbers, what went wrong, and what to fix next. Strava and Runna are encouraging; this journal is meant to be honest.

Sessions are analysed with Claude (using my Strava data) and written up here as short entries. The focus files are living documents that change as I improve.

docs.title: Running: Runna "New To Running" plan, week 7 of 8
docs.text:
1. Cadence: hold 148 spm for the whole run (stuck at ~146 on 11-17 and 11-18). Set the metronome to 152 to land at 148–150.
  2. Effort cap: keep easy-run HR under 160, and under 165 late in the run. Walk 20–30 s if over 165.
  3. Pacing: never start faster than I finish. My default "own pace" is still too hard.

docs.title: Cycling: Zone 2 base on a restored 26" MTB
docs.text:
1. Weekly long ride: ~76 min in Zone 2 (125–154 bpm) and growing ~10 min/week, toward 90–120 min. Eat at 45–60 min on rides over ~75 min.
  2. Climb control: keep flyover and bridge peaks under ~155 by shifting down early and spinning.
  3. Keep hard rides rare: events are fine; don't let event effort (HR ~160+) become normal riding.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Running calories ≈ 1 kcal per kg per km; walking ≈ half that. For rides, kJ of work ≈ kcal.
  • Apple Watch/Strava running cadence can be per leg; steps per minute = value × 2.
  • Ignore GPS max-pace spikes.
  • Calorie estimates from Strava undercount on the MTB.

Not medical advice.

docs.title: Cycling focus
docs.text: Living document: update goals, mistakes and progress as they change. Last updated 2026-11-19.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Lifelong cyclist. Rode a road bike in the US (Oct 2025 – Sep 2026, 38 rides, ~900 km).
  • Now riding a restored 26" mountain bike in Chennai (abandoned for 7 years). No plans for a road or hybrid bike for now.
  • Routes are limited by Chennai traffic and road options. Judge rides on effort and duration, not speed or distance.
  • HR zones (Strava): Z1 0–124 · Z2 125–154 · Z3 155–169 · Z4 170–184 · Z5 185+

docs.title: Active goals
docs.text: Goal Target Status Weekly long ride Zone 2, +~10 min/week toward 90–120 min 72 min @140 (11-14) → 76 min @137, 98% Z2 (11-19) ✅ Climb control Flyover and bridge peaks under ~155 Anna University flyover 157 → 145 avg (11-19); one spike to 163 on Moopanar Bridge Easy by default ~80% of rides easy (HR 125–150), ~20% hard Back on track since 11-07; 11-15 was a deliberate event

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Easy rides: HR 125–150, and you can talk the whole time.
  • Shift down early on flyovers; spin, don't stand and push.
  • Pulling away from signals: spin up in an easy gear.
  • The day before a run: keep it 30–40 min and very easy.
  • Ride-then-run back to back ("brick" workouts) not yet. Runs need fresh legs.
  • Rides over ~75 min: eat at 45–60 min (banana or dates). Red Bull isn't hydration; carry water.
  • Rest days are rest days: at most 30 min at HR under 130.
  • Front and rear lights plus something reflective for early rides.

docs.title: Recurring mistakes (from US riding history)
docs.text:
1. Every ride at the same moderately hard effort. Average HR 158–165 for hours (45 km at 158, 61 km at 162 for 3+ hours). Too hard to build base, too easy to count as real intensity.
  2. Speed plateaued for a year. ~19–21 km/h in Oct 2025 and still ~19–20 in Sep 2026.
  3. Long gaps: one ride in Feb, nothing mid-May to Aug, then only 3 rides before moving.
  4. Rode while sick (St. Patrick's Day). Don't.
  5. Bike fit: back hurt on the new road bike. Check fit and saddle height on the MTB.

docs.title: What's improving
docs.text:
• First truly easy rides in my history: 11-07 (HR 131), 11-12 (HR 137, entirely Zone 2).
  • 11-14: 72 min at HR 140 with no decoupling (first half ~16.5 km/h at 142, second half ~15.7 at 138). First evidence of aerobic durability.
  • 11-15 event: 27 km at 19.8 km/h on the MTB at HR 162, matching old road-bike speeds at a similar HR (drafting likely helped).
  • 11-19: 25 km at 19.7 km/h at HR 137 (~98% Zone 2). Event speed at 25 bpm lower HR; partly a stop-free route, but a big aerobic signal.

docs.title: Bike notes (Draco · Cosmic Eldorado 1.0L, 26" MTB)
docs.text:
Full gear list, including the new road bike (Naos, a Triban RC520): Gear.

  • Lost the bottle cage on 11-12. Bolts are backing out. Check every bolt (stem, seatpost, saddle clamp, brakes, cage mounts) and use threadlocker. Replace the cage before long rides.
  • Saddle height: slight knee bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
  • Planned: slick tyres 26 × 1.25–1.5" (~32–38 mm), budget under ₹2k. Considering aero bars for longer road rides.
  • Calories: Strava undercounts the MTB. Estimate from power (kJ ≈ kcal) plus ~0–20%.

docs.title: Running focus
docs.text: Living document: update goals, mistakes and progress as they change. Last updated 2026-11-28.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Back to running after 3+ years off. Following the Runna "New To Running" plan (week 7 of 8 as of 2026-11-17).
  • Aerobically fitter than a true beginner (lifelong cyclist), but legs and calves aren't adapted to impact yet. Classic cyclist-turned-runner trap: the engine outruns the chassis.
  • Apple Watch VO2 max estimate ~31 (Nov 2026). Low for age; should rise quickly with consistent easy running.
  • HR zones (Strava): Z1 0–124 · Z2 125–154 · Z3 155–169 · Z4 170–184 · Z5 185+, based on an assumed max HR of ~190. Observed max is at least 199 (206–207 in a rain sprint on 11-24). With max ≈ 200: Z2 ~130–162, Z3 ~162–178. Update Strava's max HR to 200.

docs.title: Active goals
docs.text: Goal Target Status Cadence 148 spm for the whole run Stuck at ~146 (11-17, 11-18); only ~29% of 11-18 at 148+. Metronome now at 152 Easy-run HR Under 160; under 165 late in the run ✅ 11-18: 92% under 160, peak 166, drift only +12 bpm Pacing Steady effort, no surges 11-18: yo-yo between ~10:00 and ~14:00/km every 0.5–0.8 km

docs.title: Rules for easy runs
docs.text:
• Conversational pace means HR, not pace. Slow down or walk to stay under the cap.
  • Make the first rep or km the slowest.
  • At 2 km into continuous runs: if HR is above 158, shorten stride and drop 20–30 s/km.
  • If HR goes over 165: walk 20–30 s, then continue.
  • Short, quick steps landing under the hips (~60 cm steps at ~11:00–11:40/km).
  • Running home after the session: walk it, or jog at the same easy pace.
  • Drink before runs; stash a bottle on the loop on hot or humid days.

docs.title: Recurring mistakes
docs.text:
1. Default pace is too fast. With no target, I settle at ~9:00–10:30/km and HR climbs into the 170s–180s (11-03, 11-04, 11-06, the 11-17 run home).
  2. Rep 1 faster than rep 2. Better since 11-11, but crept back on 11-13 (11:06 → 11:39).
  3. HR drift in the last km. Steady pace, but HR rises ~20–25 bpm (11-11, 11-17). Partly heat and humidity, partly fitness.
  4. Cadence lands below the target. 140 BPM dubstep pulled cadence to ~140; aiming at 150 lands at ~146 (11-18). Focusing on landing under the hips (11-28) made 150 feel forced while stride length stayed long. Fix: shorter steps plus arm-driven rhythm, 1-min blocks at 150–152 inside easy runs, and the metronome stepped 148 → 150 instead of jumping straight to the goal.

docs.title: Current limiter
docs.text:
• Legs, not heart. On 11-26 HR stayed flat (~155–161) while pace and legs faded in rep 2. Muscular endurance and impact tolerance lag the aerobic engine. Add leg strength twice a week and progress volume only when legs recover between runs.
  • Shoes: the Puma FuzionFit+ were worn out (compressed midsole, worn outsole, soft heel counter), and feet struggled on 11-28. Replaced 11-28 with the Nike Winflo 12 (see Gear). Watch whether feet hold up better in week 9.

docs.title: What's improving
docs.text:
• Average HR on easy sessions: 164 (11-06) → 145 (11-11) → 142 (11-13) → 152 over a longer continuous 3 km (11-17).
  • Time in Z4+: ~21 min (11-06) → 5 s (11-11) → 0 (11-13).
  • Continuous running: 2 km at HR 162 / max 184 (11-03) → 3 km at HR 152 / max 171 (11-17) → 3.75 km at HR 154 / max 166 (11-18) → 4.25 km at ~11:48/km, HR 150 (11-28).
  • HR drift in continuous runs: +25 bpm (11-17) → +12 bpm (11-18), by capping HR from the start.
  • Cadence: ~138–140 → ~146 in the main effort (11-17).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Calves got sore on 11-06. Doing calf raises (3 × 15, three times a week). Stop running for sharp or localized pain.
  • Whey protein after runs is fine; rehydrate separately with water and electrolytes.
  • Form metrics (ground contact ~330–345 ms, vertical oscillation ~9.5–10.5 cm) should improve as cadence rises. Watch the trend, not single runs.

docs.title: Gear
docs.text:
The bikes are named after stars. What I train in, how far it's gone, and when to replace it. Each session's front matter has a gear: field with one of the IDs below, and the totals table is rebuilt from those fields every time the site builds.

Last updated 2026-11-28.

docs.title: Nike Winflo 12 · winflo-12
docs.text:
• Status: active, main running shoe
  • Bought: 2026-11-28
  • Why: the most cushioned of the shoes I tried (Puma Darter Pro, adidas Adizero and Questar, Nike Pegasus 42, ASICS Gel Pulse 17). At my easy pace, protection matters more than weight or a responsive feel.
  • Replace at: ~600–800 km, or earlier if the midsole feels flat or the outsole wears through
  • Notes: first run in them is the next session. Add it to Strava as gear so distance tracks there too.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Tag every session with gear:. Use a list if a session used more than one item, e.g. gear: [winflo-12, moab].

  • Bikes: log maintenance here (date + what was done), not in session entries.

docs.text: Metric Value Distance 4.55 km Rep 1 / Rep 2 pace 9:19 → 11:05 /km Avg HR / Max HR 164 / 192 Zones Z4 37% (19:27), Z5 4% (2:01) Cadence ~140 spm while running (125 overall) Ground contact ~340–360 ms while running Vertical oscillation ~10 cm Relative Effort 122 Calories 279 (Strava)

docs.title: 2026-11-14 · Ride · First medium-distance ride in Chennai
docs.text:
Plan: Weekly long ride, Zone 2.

Conditions: 24.6°C, 89% humidity. Fasted, with one can of Red Bull.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Metric Value Distance / time 20.3 km / 72 min moving Avg speed 17.0 km/h Avg HR / Max HR 140 / 169 1st half / 2nd half ~16.5 km/h @ 142 · ~15.7 km/h @ 138 Anna University flyover (3%) avg HR 157 Relative Effort 54 Calories 367 (Strava), ~500–625 estimated

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Best base ride yet. Twice the distance of 11-12 at nearly the same HR, and no decoupling over 70+ min.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• HR spiked to 169 on flyover climbs.
  • Regular Red Bull = ~110 kcal of sugar, so not really fasted. Not hydration either.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Shift down early on flyovers; keep peaks under 155.
  • Carry water. For rides over 90 min, bring food.
  • Make this the weekly long ride; +10 min each week.

docs.title: 2026-11-15 · Ride · Race against Diabetes – Thooral 25
docs.text:
Plan: Organised charity ride (event), Pallavaram.

Conditions: 25°C, 91% humidity. Context: event, likely drafting, few stops.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Metric Value Distance / time 27.1 km / 82 min moving Avg speed 19.8 km/h Avg HR / Max HR 162 / 182 1st half / 2nd half ~19.5 km/h @ 160 · ~19.3 km/h @ 162 Relative Effort 179 Calories 625 (Strava), ~700–750 estimated

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Hard and very evenly paced. Matched old road-bike speeds (~20 km/h at HR 158–165) on a heavy MTB. Longest and fastest Chennai ride.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• Upper Zone 3 for 80 min: the same effort that kept my US speed flat for a year. Fine for an event, not as a habit.
  • Back to back with the 72-min ride the day before; no easy day between.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Rest or a very easy spin the next day.
  • Keep the next run strictly conversational, even if HR runs higher than usual.

docs.title: 2026-11-17 · Run · Continuous 3 km
docs.text:
Plan: Runna week 7. 5 min walk, 3 km continuous at conversational pace, 5 min walk.

Conditions: Two days after a hard event ride.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Metric Value Main 3 km ~11:38/km Avg HR / Max HR (3 km) 152 / 171 HR by km ~137–147 → 153–156 → 163–170 Cadence ~146 spm in the per-second data (142 lap avg) Extra after cool-down ~640 m at ~10:30/km, HR up to 180 (running home) Relative Effort 60

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: First continuous 3 km. 50% further than the 2 km on 11-03, with average HR 10 bpm lower. Cadence finally moving (~146).

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• HR drifted ~25 bpm at steady pace; last 500 m over the 165 cap.
  • The unplanned run home at "own pace" hit 180. My default pace is still too hard.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• At 2 km: if HR is above 158, shorten stride and slow 20–30 s/km. Walk 20–30 s if over 165.
  • Walk home, or jog at the same easy pace.
  • Keep the metronome; push from 146 to 148.

docs.title: 2026-11-18 · Run · Continuous 3.75 km
docs.text:
Plan: Runna New To Running, week 7. 5 min walk, 3.75 km continuous at conversational pace, 5 min walk.

Conditions: Second run in two days (ran 3 km on 11-17). Own targets: HR under 160 for the whole 3.75 km, cadence 150, ignore pace.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Metric Value Main 3.75 km ~12:39/km (47:28) Avg HR / Max HR (3.75 km) 154 / 166 Time above 160 / at 165+ ~3.7 min / ~14 s, out of 47 min HR by km 146 → 153 → 157 → 158 Pace by km ~11:53 → 13:29 → 13:12 → 13:47 (GPS glitch at the start removed) Cadence while running median ~146 spm; ≥148 only ~29% of the time Walking within the "continuous" part ~4.5 min (~9%) Relative Effort 71

Per-km figures and time-in-range are my calculations from Strava streams (~10 s resolution). A ~40 s GPS jump just after the warm-up (≈140 m at an impossible ~4:45/km with HR ~130) was removed; Strava's raw first km (~10:36) is wrong.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: HR goal essentially hit: 92% of the run under 160, peak 166, and the smallest drift of any continuous run so far (+12 bpm vs +25 on 11-17). Cadence goal missed: settled at ~146, not 150.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• Cadence plateaued at 146. It barely moved from 11-17, and you only held 148+ for about a third of the run.
  • Yo-yo pacing. The grade-adjusted pace graph swings between ~10:00 and ~14:00+/km every 0.5–0.8 km: surge, HR climbs, slow down or walk, repeat. A steady ~12:30 would have kept HR flatter with fewer walk breaks.
  • First km slightly quicker than the rest (~11:53 vs ~13:10–13:47).
  • Pace and walking were the cost of the HR cap. That's the right trade for now, but it shows how low the aerobic base still is.

docs.title: What went right
docs.text:
• Walked the cool-down home instead of running it.
  • Back-to-back days and still a lower max HR than yesterday (166 vs 171, 180 with the run home).

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Set the metronome to 152 to land at 148–150. Aiming at exactly 150 lands you at 146.
  • Hold one steady effort instead of surging: when pace drops under ~11:30/km on the watch, ease off before HR forces a walk.

docs.title: 2026-11-19 · Ride · 25 km Zone 2
docs.text:
Plan: Planned as a rest day (after runs on 11-17 and 11-18); ridden as an easy long ride instead.

Conditions: Small banana and a can of sugar-free Red Bull before; no food or gels during. Third session in three days. Legs sore afterwards.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Metric Value Distance / time 24.9 km / 76 min moving (almost no stops) Avg speed 19.7 km/h Avg HR / Max HR 137 / 163 Time in Zone 2 (125–154) ~98% 1st half / 2nd half ~20.0 km/h @ 135 · ~19.4 km/h @ 139 Anna University flyover (3%) avg HR 145 (was 157 on 11-14) Highest climb effort Moopanar Bridge segment, avg HR 155 Relative Effort 50 Calories 511 (Strava), ~650–700 estimated from power

Zone share and halves are my calculations from Strava streams (~45 s samples).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Best aerobic ride yet: event speed (19.8 km/h on 11-15 at HR 162) at HR 137, almost entirely in Zone 2. Part of the gain is a stop-free route, but the HR gap is too big to be route alone.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• It was meant to be a rest day. Run, run, then a 76-min ride: three days straight, and the legs are telling you.
  • Slight drift: speed −3%, HR +4 bpm in the second half. Mild, but it's the fuel and fatigue starting to show.
  • One spike to 163 on the Moopanar Bridge stretch; the flyover goal (under 155) held everywhere else.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Respect the rest day. If you want to ride on it, 30 min at HR under 130, not 76 min.
  • For rides over ~75 min, eat something at 45–60 min, even if the start felt fine.
  • Friday run: if the soreness is a general muscle ache, run easy and shorter; if it's sharp or in one spot (calf, shin, Achilles), skip it.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 · Swim · First swim test (pool)
docs.text:
Plan: First swim in ~2 years (last competitive swimming ~12 years ago), ahead of a pool super-sprint triathlon (300 m swim, 18 km bike, 3 km run). Breaststroke, 2 kicks per pull. Target: 100 m easy, 4 × 50 m, then 200–300 m continuous.

Conditions: 25 m pool. Arms (biceps, triceps) and front of both thighs sore afterwards.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Metric Value Distance (watch) ~450 m (18 × 25 m) Moving / elapsed 39 / 43 min Swimming bouts ~17, mostly 33–48 s (≈ one length each) Longest bouts ~100 s (≈ 50 m), twice Rests between bouts mostly 1–3+ min Pace while swimming ~2:45–3:10 per 100 m Avg HR / Max HR 131 / 165 (swimming bouts ~140–165)

Breakdown is my reading of Apple Watch lap data, which is unreliable for breaststroke with frequent stops: treat counts and paces as approximate.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: The stroke is there; the swim fitness isn't yet. Roughly half the session was resting at the wall, and the data shows no continuous 200–300 m.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• Too much rest: 1–3 min between single lengths. On race day 300 m means 12 lengths; at this pattern it would take 25+ min.
  • Heavy leg work: 2-kick breaststroke loads the quads, which is why the front of the thighs is sore on top of Thursday's ride.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Shorten rests, not effort: 6 × 50 m with 30 s rest, then try 4 lengths (100 m) non-stop.
  • Smaller, relaxed kicks with a longer glide to save the legs.
  • Race-day target: 300 m with brief wall touches (~20–30 s max), about 13–15 min.

docs.title: 2026-11-24 · Run · Continuous 3.25 km (rain)
docs.text:
Plan: Runna New To Running, week 8 of 9. 5 min walk, 3.25 km continuous at conversational pace, 5 min walk. Own target: stay in Zone 2 (≤154 bpm).

Conditions: Heavy rain started mid-run. Pushed into Zone 3 late in the run, then sprinted home instead of the walking cool-down. First run since 11-18.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Metric Value Main 3.25 km ~12:45/km, avg HR 151, max 186 Zone 2 part (first ~2.3 km) ~13:01/km, avg HR 147, 92% ≤154 Zone 3 part (next ~0.8 km) avg HR 160, max 173 Final ~160 m of the main run ~7:54/km, HR up to 186 Sprint home (~230 m, replaced cool-down) ~5:52/km, avg HR 199, max 206–207 Pace by km ~10:58 → 14:30 → 13:55 → 8:23 (last 0.24 km) Cadence while running median ~146 spm (148 in the Zone 3 part, ~162 sprinting) Relative Effort 59

Segment and split figures are my calculations from Strava streams (~20 s samples). GPS and wrist HR can both be less reliable in heavy rain.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Zone 2 discipline held for the first ~2.3 km (avg 147). The finish wasn't an easy run: Zone 3, then an all-out sprint to 206 bpm instead of the cool-down.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• First km too quick again (~10:58, then ~14:30): the yo-yo pattern from 11-18 in a new form.
  • Holding ≤154 forced a near-walking pace (~13–14:30/km). That's a sign the Zone 2 ceiling may be set too low (see below), not just low fitness.
  • Sprinting replaced the cool-down. Rain is a fair reason to get home, but it turned an easy session into a hard finish on legs that were aching last week.

docs.title: Finding: max HR is higher than Strava assumes
docs.text: Strava's zones are calculated from a max HR of ~190 (Zone 2 = 125–154). Observed maxes: 199 (May 2026 ride), 192 (11-06 run), 206–207 today. Wet-wrist spikes are possible, but 199 is already confirmed. With max HR ≈ 200, Zone 2 would be ~130–162 and Zone 3 ~162–178, which matches the 160 easy-run cap already in use.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Update max HR in Strava to 200 (conservative) so zones and Relative Effort are realistic. Re-check if 205+ shows up again in dry conditions.
  • Easy runs: cap at ~160 (new Zone 2 top), start the first km slower than you think.
  • In rain, jog home at easy effort or walk; save sprints for planned sessions.

docs.title: 2026-11-26 · Run · 2 × 2.5 km
docs.text:
Plan: Runna New To Running, week 8 of 9. 5 min walk, 2 × 2.5 km at conversational pace with 60 s walk, 5 min walk.

Conditions: Humid. Small pre-run fuel/hydration plan. Short night's sleep. Two days after the 11-24 rain run (which ended in a sprint). Legs started to give up ~1 km into rep 2.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Metric Rep 1 Rep 2 Pace ~12:32/km ~13:37/km moving (~14:14 incl. a ~1.5 min stop) Avg HR / Max HR 155 / 167 158 / 166 500 m splits 9:46 → 13:33 → 12:41 → 14:01 → 12:38 16:28* → 13:46 → 14:29 → 12:52 → 13:37 Cadence (median) ~146 spm ~146 spm
  • Total running 5 km: the most in one session so far (previous best 4 km on 11-11 and 11-13).
  • Relative Effort 81 · Strava's fastest 5K within the session: 66:22.
  • *Includes the ~1.5 min stop just after rep 2 started.

Splits are my calculations from Strava streams (~30 s samples).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Legs, not lungs. HR stayed flat at ~155–161 through both reps (Zone 2 on the corrected max-HR zones), yet rep 2 was ~1 min/km slower and the legs faded. That's muscular endurance and impact tolerance running out, on the biggest running volume yet.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• First 500 m at ~9:46/km (HR 142). The fast-start habit, again.
  • Volume jump on tired legs: 25% more running than any previous session, two days after a hard sprint finish, with legs that were aching last week.
  • Humidity and short sleep raised the cost of every km.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• First 500 m of each rep no faster than 12:30/km.
  • Leg strength twice a week (calf raises, squats, split squats; 2–3 sets of 10–15).
  • Before week 9: if legs still feel heavy, repeat this session rather than progressing.

docs.title: 2026-11-28 · Run · Continuous 4.25 km
docs.text:
Plan: Runna New To Running, week 8 of 9. 5 min walk, 4.25 km continuous at conversational pace, 5 min walk. Moved from Friday to give legs a rest day after 11-26.

Conditions: Humid; finished soaked in sweat. Felt fine aerobically; feet were the struggle. Still in the old, worn knit shoes.

Form focus: landing under the hips. Holding 150 spm with it was a struggle.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Metric Value Main 4.25 km ~11:48/km, avg HR 150, max 172 Pace by km 11:56 → 10:49 → 11:55 → 12:24 → 12:15 (last 0.27 km) HR by km 126 → 153 → 156 → 162 → 162 Time above 160 ~13 min of 50 (26%) Cadence while running median ~146 spm; ≥148 only ~22% of the time Relative Effort 50

Splits and time-in-range are my calculations from Strava streams (~25 s samples).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Longest continuous run yet, and the best one. 4.25 km at ~11:48/km and avg HR 150, versus 3.75 km at ~12:39 and HR 154 on 11-18. Further, faster, at a lower heart rate. Aerobically comfortable, as it felt. The limiter is now clearly the feet and lower legs, not the engine.

docs.title: What went wrong
docs.text:
• Km 2 surge to ~10:49/km, then HR drifted up to 160+ for the last two km. The yo-yo habit, smaller this time.
  • Cadence still ~146, only briefly at 148+. Landing under the hips while keeping the old stride length made 150 feel forced: the stride has to shorten for cadence to rise.
  • Feet struggled, in shoes that are worn out and give little support.

docs.title: Fix for next time
docs.text:
• Replace the running shoes before week 9's longer runs. Done the same day: Nike Winflo 12.
  • Cadence: keep the land-under-hips cue but take smaller, quieter steps, and drive the rhythm with a compact arm swing. Do 4–5 × 1 min at 150–152 inside easy runs, and set the metronome to 148 for the next two runs before moving to 150.
  • Hold km 2 at the same pace as km 1; ease off whenever the watch shows under ~11:30/km.
  • Rehydrate with ORS or salted buttermilk after humid runs; you lose more than a litre.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• All three runs were done too hard. Avg HR 157–164, max up to 192, ~21 min in Z4–5 on 11-06.
  • Each run started at my default ~9:00/km and faded. Rep 2 was slower at a higher HR every time.
  • Relative Effort climbed 43 → 82 → 122 while distance only grew from 2 km to 3.5 km.
  • Bright spot: 11-07 was the first truly easy ride in my history (HR 131).
  • Calves got sore on 11-06.

docs.title: Goals set for next week
docs.text:
1. Cap easy-run HR at 160 (165 late); walk if over.
  2. Rep 1 no faster than rep 2.
  3. Cadence toward 148 (shorter, quicker steps).
  4. Rides: stay in Zone 2, build duration.

docs.title: Goal check
docs.text: Goal Result Easy-run HR ≤160 (165 late) ⚠️ Avg HR down to 142–145 and Z4 near zero, but rep 2 still peaked at 170–175 Rep 1 ≤ rep 2 ✅ 11-11 · ❌ 11-13 (11:06 → 11:39) Cadence → 148 ❌ Stuck at ~138–140 (dubstep half-time trap) Rides in Zone 2, building duration ✅ 40 min → 72 min, no decoupling

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Biggest change of the block: same runs at ~20 bpm lower HR than week 45.
  • Week 6 of the Runna plan completed.
  • Rides: 11-12 entirely Zone 2; 11-14 was the best base ride yet (20 km at HR 140); 11-15 was a hard charity event (27 km at HR 162), evenly paced.
  • Lost the bottle cage on 11-12. Check the bike's bolts.

docs.title: Adjustments for next week
docs.text:
1. Cadence becomes the #1 running goal: use a metronome at 148 for full reps.
  2. Continuous runs: check HR at 2 km; slow down early rather than walk late.
  3. Recovery: no easy day between the 11-14 long ride and the 11-15 event. Take it easy into the next run.
  4. Long ride: aim for ~80 min in Zone 2; flyover peaks under 155.
